name: Maastricht University
about: A research university in a small city wedged between Belgium and Germany, teaching almost everything through problem-based learning: small tutorial groups working through cases rather than lectures. It also holds University College Maastricht, a 250-place liberal-arts college that admits by interview — so at Maastricht an IB student can see all three Dutch entry regimes side by side.
knownFor: Liberal arts at University College Maastricht

languageOfInstruction.note: Maastricht teaches a majority of its bachelor programmes in English, which is unusual among Dutch research universities and is exactly what the internationalisation bill is aimed at. Check in autumn 2026 that the programme you want is still English-taught for September 2027.

notes: Maastricht publishes its additional subject requirements in one table covering every programme, per diploma, in IB terms — the same pattern as TU Delft and the same conclusion for ADR 0002: nothing to translate.

The three programmes recorded here were chosen because they differ in admission regime rather than in subject: International Business is numerus fixus and closes 15 January; University College Maastricht is selective on its own dates of 1 February and 1 April; Data Science and Artificial Intelligence is neither, and closes 1 May. All three are at one university.

Not established: whether the International Business selection weighting and the International Classroom requirement carry unchanged into the 2027 round. The programme page still described 2026-2027 when it was read.
